paragraphs: Pandora is a company from Denmark. It makes rings and other small pieces that people wear. On November 4, it shared its results for the third quarter of 2026. The news site RetailBoss reported them the same day. The main number was organic growth of 6%. Pandora also revised its goals for the full year.

What is organic growth? It leaves out changes in the value of money between countries. In other words, it tries to show the real growth of the business itself. Pandora's growth came from two distinct parts. The first part was like-for-like growth of 4%. This measure compares sales in the same stores, so new stores do not count. The second part, about 2%, came from more stores and other factors. So growth did not come solely from opening new stores. Revenue for the quarter was 6.694 billion Danish kroner. Revenue is all the money a company takes in from its sales.

Growth was far from equal around the world. Asia Pacific was the remarkable one, with like-for-like growth of 20%. Latin America came next, at 6%. North America grew 3%. The region that covers Europe, the Middle East and Africa grew only 1%. These are distinct markets, and they moved at very different speeds.

There was also news about profit. The profit margin that Pandora reported was 15.9%. The margin is the part of each sale that a company keeps as profit. However, this number needs care. Part of it came from a one-time payment. Pandora received a partial refund of the tax it paid on goods that it brought into the United States. This partial refund added 3.7 percentage points to the margin. That is a meaningful amount. Pandora acknowledged that, without the refund, its margin was broadly flat compared with a year earlier.

Pandora revised its growth goal for the year. It now expects organic growth of 2% to 3% for 2026. Before, it expected 0% to 3%. So the bottom of the range moved up, while the top stayed the same. It also changed its margin goal for the year to 22.5% to 23%, from 22% to 23%.
Not every number was strong. In October, like-for-like growth was only 1%. The company acknowledged that it ran fewer special offers that month. Those fewer offers held the number down.

Looking ahead, Pandora is preparing changes. One area of emphasis is the design of its products. Another is marketing. The company wants to adapt its marketing so that it feels meaningful to buyers in each local market. A third area of emphasis is the experience inside its stores, which it also plans to adapt.

The results highlight one point. The goals for the year are now stronger, and that is good news. Nevertheless, the higher margin did not come solely from the business itself. It partially came from the one-time refund. That demonstrates why readers should also look at the margin without the refund.
